name: Movavi
editorial: For Movavi, use footage from a phone and a camera in the same test project. Confirm that trimming, stabilization, and title placement survive a change of aspect ratio. Export once for a vertical platform and once for a presentation screen; a smooth preview is not enough if the final file changes color or crops captions. If a project depends on a particular effect, check whether that effect belongs to the editor or to a separately licensed pack. Ask a collaborator to reopen the saved project on another machine before choosing the plan. Movavi is worth evaluating when your work centers on desktop video editing. Start with a short social clip and a longer tutorial; these two deliverables expose different constraints, so a single polished demo is a poor buying test. For the first, write down the time spent preparing source material, making the initial cut, and correcting mistakes. For the second, repeat the process with a fresh asset rather than reusing a finished template. This gives you a practical comparison of effort across routine and less predictable work. Pay particular attention to timeline exports, caption revisions, and handoff formats. Ask a colleague to open the exported result on another device and note any missing captions, clipped audio, font substitution, or awkward pacing. Keep the source file so you can measure how painful a late revision would be. A workflow that feels fast for one person may slow down when another person has to review it. Before paying, check whether the installed edition covers the export settings you actually need. Read the current checkout and license terms directly on the merchant site, since plan names and entitlements can change. Save a dated screenshot of the offer and renewal conditions, then compare the total cost over the period you will actually use the tool. If you are buying for a team, assign one person to test access, permissions, and export ownership. This evaluation is our editorial method, not a claim that a discount is available today.
refund_policy: Check current merchant terms; not independently verified.
